items.title: Three New Grounds: Applied and Sustained Thought

items.zh: 已說意地。云何有尋有伺地？云何無尋唯伺地？云何無尋無伺地？
items.en: The Mind Stage has now been explained. What is the Ground of Applied and Sustained Thought? What is the Ground of No Applied Thought but Only Sustained Thought? What is the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought?

items.zh: 總嗢拕南曰：界、相、如理、不如理、雜染等起最為後。
items.en: The summary verse states: realm, mark, what accords with reason and what does not; defilement and its arising come last.

items.zh: 如是三地，略以五門施設建立。一、界施設建立，二、相施設建立，三、如理作意施設建立，四、不如理作意施設建立，五、雜染等起施設建立。
items.en: These three grounds, briefly stated, are established through five gateways: first, establishing the realms; second, establishing their marks; third, establishing what accords with reason; fourth, establishing what does not accord with reason; fifth, establishing defilement and its arising.

items.zh: 云何界施設建立？
items.en: What is the establishment of the realms?

items.title: Eight Ways to Establish the Three Realms

items.zh: 別嗢拕南曰：數、處、量、壽、受用、生、自體、因緣果分別。
items.en: A further summary verse states: number, place, measure, lifespan, enjoyment, birth; own body, and the analysis of cause, condition, and result.

items.zh: 當知界建立由八種相。一、數建立，二、處建立，三、有情量建立，四、有情壽建立，五、有情受用建立，六、生建立，七、自體建立，八、因緣果建立。
items.en: It should be understood that the realms are established through eight aspects: first, establishing their number; second, establishing their places; third, establishing beings' physical measure; fourth, establishing beings' lifespan; fifth, establishing beings' enjoyment; sixth, establishing their birth; seventh, establishing their own body; eighth, establishing cause, condition, and result.

items.title: The Three Realms, and What Falls Outside Them

items.zh: 云何數建立？略有三界。謂欲界、色界、無色界。如是三種，名墮攝界。
items.en: What is the establishing of the realms? Briefly, there are three realms: the desire realm, the form realm, and the formless realm. These three are called the realms comprised within conditioned falling.

items.zh: 非墮攝界者，謂方便，并薩迦耶滅，及無戲論無漏界。
items.en: What is not comprised within falling is: skilful means, together with the cessation of the view of a perishable body, and the uncontaminated realm free of conceptual elaboration.

items.title: How the Desire Realm and the First Dhyāna Both Get Called "With Thought"

items.zh: 此中欲界及色界初靜慮，除靜慮中間若定、若生，名有尋有伺地。
items.en: Here, the desire realm, together with the first dhyāna of the form realm — excluding the intermediate dhyāna, whether as a meditative attainment or as a rebirth — is called the Ground of Applied and Sustained Thought.

items.zh: 即靜慮中間若定、若生，名無尋唯伺地。隨一有情，由修此故，得為大梵。從第二靜慮，餘有色界及無色界全，名無尋無伺地。
items.en: The intermediate dhyāna itself, whether as attainment or as rebirth, is called the Ground of No Applied Thought but Only Sustained Thought. Any given being who cultivates this may, through it, become a Great Brahmā. From the second dhyāna onward — the whole of the remaining form realm and the entire formless realm — is called the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought.

items.zh: 此中由離尋伺欲道理故，說名無尋無伺地，不由不現行故。所以者何？未離欲界欲者，由教導作意差別故，於一時間亦有無尋無伺意現行。
items.en: Here, it is by reason of having become free of the craving for applied and sustained thought that it is called the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought — not because such thought fails to actually occur. Why is this? Because one who has not yet become free of the desire realm's craving may, through a teacher's specific instruction in attention, temporarily manifest a mind without applied or sustained thought.

items.zh: 已離尋伺欲者，亦有尋伺現行。如出彼定、及生彼者。
items.en: One who has become free of the craving for applied and sustained thought may nonetheless still manifest applied and sustained thought — as when emerging from that very meditative absorption, or when reborn into it.

items.title: Even the Liberated Mind Can Be Classified as "With Thought"

items.zh: 若無漏界有為定所攝初靜慮，亦名有尋有伺地。依尋伺處法，緣真如為境入此定故，不由分別現行故。餘如前說。
items.en: If the uncontaminated realm is comprised within a conditioned meditative attainment belonging to the first dhyāna, this too is called the Ground of Applied and Sustained Thought. This is because one enters this absorption by relying on the very same applied-and-sustained-thought basis, taking suchness itself as the object — not because ordinary conceptual discrimination is actually occurring. The rest should be understood as already explained.

items.zh: 處所建立者，於欲界中有三十六處。謂八大那落迦。何等為八？一、等活，二、黑繩，三、眾合，四、號叫，五、大號叫，六、燒熱，七、極燒熱，八、無間。此諸大那落迦處，廣十千踰繕那。此外復有八寒那落迦處。何等為八？一、皰那落迦，二、皰裂那落迦，三、𠿒哳詀那落迦，四、郝郝凡那落迦，五、虎虎凡那落迦，六、青蓮那落迦，七、紅蓮那落迦，八、大紅蓮那落迦。從此下三萬二千踰繕那，至等活那落迦。從此復隔四千踰繕那，有餘那落迦。如等活大那落迦處，初寒那落迦處亦爾。從此復隔二千踰繕那，有餘那落迦應知。
items.en: As for the establishment of places: in the desire realm there are thirty-six places. First, the eight great hells. Which eight? First, Reviving; second, Black Rope; third, Crushing; fourth, Wailing; fifth, Great Wailing; sixth, Burning; seventh, Intensely Burning; eighth, Uninterrupted. Each of these great hells is ten thousand yojanas wide. Besides these there are eight cold hells. Which eight? First, the Blister hell; second, the Burst Blister hell; third, the Aṭaṭa hell; fourth, the Hahava hell; fifth, the Huhuva hell; sixth, the Blue Lotus hell; seventh, the Red Lotus hell; eighth, the Great Red Lotus hell. From here, thirty-two thousand yojanas below, lies the Reviving hell. Four thousand yojanas further down lie the other hells. As with the place of the great Reviving hell, so too with the first cold hell. It should be understood that two thousand yojanas further down lie the other cold hells.

items.zh: 又有餓鬼處所。
items.en: Further, there are the places where hungry ghosts dwell.

items.zh: 又有非天處所。
items.en: Further, there are the places where asuras dwell.

items.title: Where Animals, Humans, and the Continents Fit

items.zh: 傍生即與人天同處，故不別建立。復有四大洲，如前說。復有八中洲。
items.en: Animals dwell in the very same places as humans and gods, and are therefore not separately established. Further, there are the four great continents, as already explained. Further, there are eight intermediate continents.

items.title: The Six Heavens of the Desire Realm

items.zh: 又欲界天有六處。一、四大王眾天，二、三十三天，三、時分天，四、知足天，五、樂化天，六、他化自在天。
items.en: Further, the desire realm's heavens comprise six places: first, the heaven of the Four Great Kings; second, the Heaven of the Thirty-Three; third, the Heaven of Time's Divisions; fourth, the Heaven of Contentment; fifth, the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation; sixth, the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations.

items.zh: 復有摩羅天宮，即他化自在天攝，然處所高勝。
items.en: Further, there is the palace of Māra, comprised within the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations, though its own location stands higher and more excellent.

items.title: Solitary and Nearby Hells, and the Desire Realm's Total: Thirty-Six

items.zh: 復有獨一那落迦、近邊那落迦，即大那落迦及寒那落迦。以近邊故，不別立處。又於人中，亦有一分獨一那落迦可得。
items.en: Further, there are the solitary hells and the neighbouring hells — these belong to the great hells and the cold hells already described. Because they lie nearby, no separate place is established for them. Further, even among humans, a portion of solitary hells can be found.

items.zh: 如尊者取菉豆子說：我見諸有情，燒然、極燒然、遍極燒然，總一燒然聚。
items.en: As the Venerable One Who Took the Mung Bean said: "I see beings burning, intensely burning, entirely and intensely burning — a single mass of flame altogether."

items.zh: 如是等三十六處，總名欲界。
items.en: All these places, thirty-six in number, are together called the desire realm.

items.title: Eighteen Places in the Form Realm

items.zh: 復次，色界有十八處。
items.en: Further, the form realm comprises eighteen places.

items.title: The First Three Dhyānas' Nine Heavens

items.zh: 謂梵眾天、梵前益天、大梵天，此三由軟中上品熏修初靜慮故。少光天、無量光天、極淨光天，此三由軟中上品熏修第二靜慮故。
items.en: Namely: Brahmā's Retinue, Brahmā's Ministers, and Great Brahmā — these three exist because of cultivating the first dhyāna to a weak, middling, or superior degree. Lesser Light, Boundless Light, and Utmost Pure Light — these three exist because of cultivating the second dhyāna to a weak, middling, or superior degree.

items.zh: 少淨天、無量淨天、遍淨天，此三由軟中上品熏修第三靜慮故。
items.en: Lesser Purity, Boundless Purity, and Universal Purity — these three exist because of cultivating the third dhyāna to a weak, middling, or superior degree.

items.title: The Fourth Dhyāna: Ordinary Beings, and the Heaven of No Perception

items.zh: 無雲天、福生天、廣果天，此三由軟中上品熏修第四靜慮故。無想天即廣果攝，無別處所。
items.en: Cloudless, Merit-Born, and Vast Fruit — these three exist because of cultivating the fourth dhyāna to a weak, middling, or superior degree. The Heaven of No Perception is comprised within Vast Fruit, having no separate place of its own.

blocks.text: Fascicle 4 begins the third, fourth, and fifth of the seventeen stages: the **Ground with Applied and Sustained Thought** (有尋有伺地), the **Ground without Applied but with Sustained Thought** (無尋唯伺地), and the **Ground without Either** (無尋無伺地). The treatise treats them together, under five headings, and the first heading, "establishing the realms", takes up all of fascicle 4. So we begin a survey of the three realms: their places, the size and lifespan of their beings, and their pleasures and pains.

Two passages are missing from Ru-Yi's translation (now supplied in our own translation, marked as ours): the question "What is the establishment of the realms?" (0294b19) and, more importantly, 0294c09–c20, the list of the thirty-six places of the desire realm. It names the eight great hells (Reviving, Black Rope, Crushing, Wailing, Great Wailing, Burning, Intensely Burning, and Uninterrupted), the eight cold hells, the ghost and asura realms, the four continents with their eight intermediate continents, and the six desire-realm heavens.

The three new grounds are defined by two mental factors we met in Day 3's list. **Applied thought** (尋, *vitarka*) and **sustained thought** (伺, *vicāra*). Venerable Miào Jìng: applied thought "moves hurriedly over its object", roughly seeking its features; sustained thought "moves slowly through it", examining carefully. Think of searching a room for something and then studying what you found.
The three grounds are set out through five gateways: the realms, their marks, what accords with reason, what does not, and defilement and its arising.
The realms are established through eight aspects: number, place, beings' size, lifespan, enjoyment, birth, own body, and cause-condition-result. Fascicle 4 works through them in order.

The three realms are "comprised within falling" (墮攝). Venerable Miào Jìng: 墮 means dropping down, "like a bird falling from the sky", and 攝 can be read as "bondage". What lies outside falling is the path, the cessation of the view of a self, and the uncontaminated realm free of elaboration: the noble truths of path and cessation, and nirvāṇa.

items: **With applied and sustained thought**: the desire realm and the first dhyāna.
**Without applied but with sustained thought**: the "intermediate dhyāna" between the first and second; one who cultivates it may become a Great Brahmā (Day 10).
**Without either**: the second dhyāna and everything above.

blocks.text: The key qualification: the third ground is named "by reason of having become free of the craving for applied and sustained thought", not because such thought never occurs. Both teachers stress this. Someone not yet free of that craving may be momentarily without thought; someone free of it still thinks after emerging from meditation. The stage is defined by detachment, not by the momentary state.

Venerable Miào Jìng adds that ordinary desire-realm thought is thought of desire, hostility, and harm, while first-dhyāna thought is of renunciation, non-hostility, and non-harm: the same faculty, opposite contents.

Hungry ghosts and asuras have their own places. Animals do not, "because animals dwell in the very same places as humans and gods". Master Cháng Bǎi: where people live there are cats, dogs, and ants. Beside each of the four continents are two intermediate continents. Māra's palace is counted within the highest desire heaven, though it stands higher. There are also "solitary hells" among humans, quoted from Mahāmaudgalyāyana's accounts. In all, the desire realm has **thirty-six** places.

Each of the first three dhyānas has three heavens, produced by cultivating that dhyāna to a weak, middling, or superior degree. The fourth dhyāna has heavens for ordinary beings, including the **Heaven of No Perception** (無想天), which "is comprised within Vast Fruit, having no separate place". Venerable Miào Jìng explains it: practitioners in the fourth dhyāna decide perception is the problem and suppress it, and are reborn without perception for a long time, which is not liberation. Tomorrow we read the heavens reserved for noble ones.

quiz.q: According to Venerable Miào Jìng, how do applied thought (尋) and sustained thought (伺) differ?
options: applied thought "moves hurriedly over its object," roughly seeking; sustained thought "moves slowly through it," examining carefully
applied thought is wholesome, sustained thought unwholesome
applied thought belongs to the eye-consciousness, sustained thought to the ear
applied thought is past, sustained thought future
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The mind 'moves hurriedly over its object,' not so calm … roughly, generally seeking the object's features — that is applied thought"; "sustained thought is not so hurried on the object — 'moving slowly through it,' examining, observing, reflecting carefully." Master Cháng Bǎi likewise: applied thought is coarse investigation, sustained thought fine examination. Both are indeterminate factors that can be wholesome or not, so B is wrong.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through which eight aspects are the realms established?
options: birth, ageing, sickness, death, separation, encountering, not getting, the aggregates
number, place, beings' measure, lifespan, enjoyment, birth, own body, and cause-condition-result
quiz.why: "First, establishing their number; second, their places; third, beings' physical measure; fourth, beings' lifespan; fifth, beings' enjoyment; sixth, their birth; seventh, their own body; eighth, cause, condition, and result." Fascicle 4 stops partway through the fifth; the rest follow in fascicle 5. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is a complete survey of a being's situation, laid out before the treatise discusses how to get free.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what does the Ground of Applied and Sustained Thought include?
options: the desire realm and the whole form realm
the desire realm and the form realm's first dhyāna, excluding the intermediate dhyāna (whether as attainment or rebirth)
quiz.why: "The desire realm, together with the first dhyāna of the form realm — excluding the intermediate dhyāna, whether as a meditative attainment or as a rebirth — is called the Ground of Applied and Sustained Thought." Venerable Miào Jìng: the intermediate dhyāna lies between the first and second; "attainment" is achieving it in this life, "rebirth" is being born there after death. Master Cháng Bǎi: though free of desire, the first dhyāna still applies thought to counter the desire realm's pull, so it remains in this ground.

quiz.q: What, according to the treatise, is the basis for naming the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought, and how do both teachers stress it?
options: whether one is free of the craving for such thought, not whether it occurs — one not yet free can be momentarily thought-free, and one who is free still has thought on emerging from absorption
quiz.why: "It is by reason of having become free of the craving for applied and sustained thought that it is called the Ground Without Applied or Sustained Thought — not because such thought fails to actually occur." Venerable Miào Jìng: "So having or not having desire is the boundary between the grounds"; a child without desire, or someone in dreamless sleep, is not thereby in this ground. Master Cháng Bǎi: one still in desire can, under a teacher's guidance, be momentarily thought-free and still belong to the desire realm's ground. A is exactly the intuition corrected here.

quiz.q: Why, according to the treatise, is no separate place established for animals?
options: because animals dwell in the very same places as humans and gods
because there are too few animals
quiz.why: "Animals dwell in the very same places as humans and gods, and are therefore not separately established." Master Cháng Bǎi: where people live there are cats, dogs, cockroaches, and ants, and there are birds in the heavens too. Venerable Miào Jìng: the older rendering "domestic beasts" and Xuánzàng's "sideways-born" mean the same.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many places make up the desire realm in total?
options: thirty-six — eight great hells, eight cold hells, the ghost realm, the asura realm, four continents, eight intermediate continents, and six heavens
quiz.why: "All these places, thirty-six in number, are together called the desire realm." The *Pixunji*: eight great hells, eight cold hells, the ghost realm, the asura realm, four great continents, eight intermediate continents, and six heavens — Venerable Miào Jìng adds them up: 8 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 4 + 8 + 6. A is the form realm's count. (Note: the Ru-Yi translation omits the passage that names the great and cold hells and their depths.)

quiz.q: According to the treatise, where is the Heaven of No Perception?
options: comprised within Vast Fruit, with no separate place of its own
quiz.why: "The Heaven of No Perception is comprised within Vast Fruit, having no separate place of its own." Venerable Miào Jìng: outsiders practising the fourth dhyāna decide perception is the problem and suppress it there; succeeding, they reach this heaven. Master Cháng Bǎi: it is the brāhmaṇas' highest "nirvāṇa," in truth only another conditioned result. C is wrong: the pure abodes belong to noble ones.
